newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht firms late, interbank rate eases.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht firms late, interbank rate eases.

text.p: The Thai baht firmed slightly late on Tuesday in the local and offshore markets as dollar buying waned in line with a weaker tone in the US unit, dealers said.
The baht was quoted around 25.810/25/840 baht per dollar in the onshore market compared with 25.830/25.850 early in the day. The baht was traded at a high of 25.85 baht in the morning, they added.
The central bank set the midrate at 25.80 baht to the dollar on Tuesday.

The two-tier money market system imposed by the central bank last week to stave of offshore speculative attack on the baht remained intact and the central bank said on Tuesday that it would review it from time to time.
Under the system, the Bank of Thailand cut baht supplies to the offshore players by asking Thailand-based commercial bank not to lend baht to foreign buyers.
The overnight interbank rate eased further to 10.00-11.50 pecent late Tuesday from 11.00-12.50 percent ealier as the market was flushed with liquidity.

"The maturities of 30-billion-baht central bank paper this week and money parked in the system for corporate tax payments due later this month has substantially increased liquidity in the market," said a dealer from a major Thai bank.
"We expected the rate to be around this level or slightly lower for the rest of the week," he added.
The baht-dollar swap premium for one-month tenor was quoted around 14/15 satangs per dollar (bid/offer) in onshore market and 35/45 satangs in the offshore market.
